cohort: 96 women in labor who had a history of previous cesarean section and were attempting a vaginal birth
finding: Continuing midwifery care was associated with shorter labor lengths, higher vaginal birth rates, and lower postpartum hemorrhage rates compared to standard maternity care in women attempting vaginal birth after cesarean.
mod_finding: Women receiving continuing midwifery care had a significantly higher vaginal birth rate compared to those receiving standard maternity care.
